data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Manual (DM) establishes the process for how the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) manages licensed information technology (IT) software and how to determine payment for fewer or additional licenses using an annual reconciliation process, in accordance with the enterprise agreement between the vendor and USDA.

This DM applies to USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, volunteers, and others working for, or on behalf of, USDA who manage USDA-supplied computer hardware and software in the performance of their duties on behalf of USDA.
policy_statements.target: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, volunteers, and others working for, or on behalf of, USDA
conditions: who manage USDA-supplied computer hardware and software in the performance of their duties on behalf of USDA

policy_statements.source_text: The Federal Government spends a significant amount annually on software acquisitions to enable business or mission functions.
policy_statements.actor_name: Federal Government

policy_statements.source_text: It is incumbent on USDA to ensure practices as a purchaser and user of licensed software are carried out effectively, efficiently, and in compliance with all applicable legislation and copyrights, for example Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), Public Law (P.L.) 113-291 § 831-837; Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA), 44 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 3551, et seq.; and Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Memorandum M-16-12, Category Management Policy 16-1: Improving the Acquisition and Management of Common Information Technology: Software Licensing.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA
policy_statements.target: practices as a purchaser and user of licensed software
cross_references: Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), Public Law (P.L.) 113-291 § 831-837
Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA), 44 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 3551, et seq.
Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Memorandum M-16-12, Category Management Policy 16-1: Improving the Acquisition and Management of Common Information Technology: Software Licensing

policy_statements.source_text: USDA acquires software licenses and must only use the software and documentation in accordance with applicable license agreements.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA
conditions: in accordance with applicable license agreements

policy_statements.source_text: USDA does not own such software or its related documentation.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA
policy_statements.target: such software or its related documentation

policy_statements.source_text: Except as specifically authorized by a software licenser in an agreement, USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, volunteers, and others who are working for, or on behalf of, USDA and are authorized to use USDA-supplied licensed software in performing their functions are prohibited from reproducing licensed software or related documentation.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, volunteers, and others
conditions: Except as specifically authorized by a software licenser in an agreement
who are working for, or on behalf of, USDA and are authorized to use USDA-supplied licensed software in performing their functions

policy_statements.source_text: Licensed agreements, licensed software means that “free software” is prohibited from installation on USDA systems without approved waiver requests.
conditions: without approved waiver requests

policy_statements.source_text: Penalties will apply to any violation of this requirement.

USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices are responsible for distributing and maintaining software license agreements reflecting their purchased/installed software licenses that should be available for reference to determine if copies can be made, for example, for backup or archival purposes, and to assure compliance with all provisions of the software agreement.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: software license agreements reflecting their purchased/installed software licenses

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, and others working for, or on behalf of, USDA and are authorized to purchase software outside of the standard acquisition procedures for USDA are responsible for the licensing, compliance, maintenance, service, and annual “true-up” for software purchases.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, and others working for, or on behalf of, USDA
policy_statements.target: licensing, compliance, maintenance, service, and annual “true-up” for software purchases
conditions: are authorized to purchase software outside of the standard acquisition procedures for USDA

policy_statements.source_text: The annual “true-up” is a process for reconciling licenses purchased by USDA against those that are installed on USDA computer systems.
Respect for intellectual effort and creativity is vital.
This principle applies to works of all authors and publishers in media.
Because software is easily reproduced, respect for the work and creativity of others is especially critical.
USDA has both a legal and ethical responsibility to prevent unauthorized duplication and distribution of software.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA
policy_statements.target: unauthorized duplication and distribution of software

policy_statements.source_text: This DM is effective immediately and shall remain in effect until superseded or expiration;
conditions: until superseded or expiration

policy_statements.source_text: The overarching policies and roles and responsibilities for this DM are provided in Departmental Regulation (DR) 3160-001, Licensed Information Technology (IT) Software;
cross_references: Departmental Regulation (DR) 3160-001, Licensed Information Technology (IT) Software

policy_statements.source_text: If a specific provision of this DM is superseded by another regulation or otherwise invalidated by external laws, directives, or standard practices the remaining provisions shall not be invalidated; and
conditions: If a specific provision of this DM is superseded by another regulation or otherwise invalidated by external laws, directives, or standard practices

policy_statements.source_text: The term “agency” or phrase “agency and staff office,” unless otherwise noted in this directive, will be considered to encompass the Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices of USDA.
policy_statements.target: term “agency” or phrase “agency and staff office,”
conditions: unless otherwise noted in this directive

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Area Assistant CIOs, Agency and Staff Office IT Directors, and Contractor IT Leads will:
Communicate the terms and restrictions of IT licensed software;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Area Assistant CIOs, Agency and Staff Office IT Directors, and Contractor IT Leads

policy_statements.source_text: Make clear USDA’s policy and penalties for the installation and use of free and/or unauthorized free software; and
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Area Assistant CIOs, Agency and Staff Office IT Directors, and Contractor IT Leads

policy_statements.source_text: Include a statement along with the yearly reconciliation process certification that users of computer software have been made aware of the terms and conditions of an acquired software product’s license agreement and to abide by such agreement and the associated penalties for not adhering to the terms of agreement.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Area Assistant CIOs, Agency and Staff Office IT Directors, and Contractor IT Leads

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, volunteers, and others working for, or on behalf of, USDA using reconciliation software other than approved and authorized software programs or applications will receive written approval from the USDA Client Experience Center (CEC) Category Management Office (CMO) before using and submitting their reconciliation report.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, volunteers, and others working for, or on behalf of, USDA
policy_statements.target: written approval from the USDA Client Experience Center (CEC) Category Management Office (CMO)
conditions: using reconciliation software other than approved and authorized software programs or applications
before using and submitting their reconciliation report

policy_statements.source_text: End users who provide information services and products, including instruction in the use of software resources, will refrain from copying and distributing software and related documentation, except as specifically authorized by licensed agreement, but also clearly inform users they are responsible licensees of such proprietary products.
policy_statements.actor_name: End users
conditions: who provide information services and products, including instruction in the use of software resources
except as specifically authorized by licensed agreement

policy_statements.source_text: This section provides an overview of the procedures for managing USDA licensed IT software and how to determine payment for additional licenses during the annual reconciliation process, in accordance with the enterprise agreement between the vendor and USDA to include the use of approved configuration management tools (or similar approved products), to track and manage licensed software.
policy_statements.target: procedures for managing USDA licensed IT software

policy_statements.source_text: To get an accurate picture of the versions and licenses deployed across the environment, many USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices have enabled client software on hardware devices that can be leveraged to pull asset reports that detail the versions and quantities of software deployed on desktops, laptops, and servers.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: These reports are used to develop and confirm procurement requirements to ensure that software contracts are licensed appropriately.

Requirement: On an annual basis, each March, the USDA Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) approved reconciliation software is used to identify all installed software products across USDA in support of the required yearly reconciliation (or subsequent requirement name).
policy_statements.target: all installed software products across USDA
conditions: On an annual basis, each March

policy_statements.source_text: As part of the reconciliation process, the Mission Area, agency, and staff offices Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) provides the CMO (or subsequent name) with the initial number of installed enterprise software licenses.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, and staff offices Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR)
conditions: As part of the reconciliation process

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must pay for any additional software licenses installed on servers, desktops, laptops, or any device that exceeds the initial number of licenses purchased and/or the additional licenses paid for from a previous reconciliation.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: any additional software licenses installed on servers, desktops, laptops, or any device
conditions: that exceeds the initial number of licenses purchased and/or the additional licenses paid for from a previous reconciliation

policy_statements.source_text: A major benefit to the reconciliation is that customers automatically receive software upgrades.
policy_statements.actor_name: customers

policy_statements.source_text: Annual Reconciliation Process Inputs
USDA IT software license reconciliation numbers are based on enterprise software agreements; and
Yearly reconciliation pricing based on enterprise software agreements.

USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices are responsible for installing server, desktop, and laptop software and running annual software reconciliation reports that compare installed software quantities against authorized software quantities.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: When installed software quantities exceed the amount authorized under the contract USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices are required to:
conditions: When installed software quantities exceed the amount authorized under the contract

policy_statements.source_text: Remove the exceeded quantities;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Provide authorized funding to pay for the additional installed software; and
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Forward the authorized funding to the OCIO-CEC-Category Management Office (hereby referred to as CMO staff).
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: The CMO staff prepares the formal request with the authorized funding and coordinates with USDA Mission Area Senior Contracting Officials (MASCO) to authorize and pay for the additional licenses.
policy_statements.actor_name: CMO staff
policy_statements.target: formal request with the authorized funding

policy_statements.source_text: Annual Reconciliation Process Outputs
USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices complete the formal request and funding authorization which are then submitted to CMO staff at: ITCategoryManagement@ocio.usda.gov.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Reconciliation funding memorandums are retained by CMO staff overseeing enterprise licensed software contracts.
policy_statements.actor_name: CMO staff

policy_statements.source_text: Licensed Software Reconciliation Sub-Process Steps
USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices shall provide oversight in:
Performing an annual reconciliation process; and
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Running the approved software management tool(s) to determine how many licensed IT software copies are installed.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Determine the number of additional licenses to be purchased by referencing the previous reconciliation licenses spreadsheet.
policy_statements.target: number of additional licenses to be purchased

policy_statements.source_text: Add the base licenses plus reconciliation licenses already purchased.
policy_statements.target: base licenses plus reconciliation licenses already purchased

policy_statements.source_text: If the configuration report shows more licenses installed than paid for, then the USDA Mission Area, agency, or staff office must pay the reconciliation amount.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Area, agency, or staff office
conditions: If the configuration report shows more licenses installed than paid for

policy_statements.source_text: The Yearly Reconciliation is completed when:
An accurate count of approved and authorized software installed is completed;
A comparison of reconciliation process software quantity with the software contract is completed and provided to the CMO and the MASCO; and
Payment is executed by the MASCO for overage or refund or credit requested for being under the contract maximum.
policy_statements.actor_name: MASCO
conditions: for overage or refund or credit requested for being under the contract maximum

policy_statements.source_text: Users will find supporting documents at the Category Management Interest Group SharePoint site.
policy_statements.actor_name: Users
cross_references: Category Management Interest Group SharePoint site

policy_statements.source_text: CMO staff will verify that the process is being performed by annually reviewing this document and the artifacts that are the output of this document.
policy_statements.actor_name: CMO staff

policy_statements.source_text: To validate this process, CMO staff will have the verification document peer reviewed by relevant subject matter experts (SME) before approval.
policy_statements.actor_name: CMO staff
conditions: before approval

policy_statements.source_text: Afterward, its continued validity will be determined during periodic management reviews.
conditions: during periodic management reviews

policy_statements.source_text: CMO staff will include training in this process for appropriate staff as part of its comprehensive training program.
policy_statements.actor_name: CMO staff
policy_statements.target: training in this process for appropriate staff

policy_statements.source_text: CMO staff will sustain this process by conducting routine management reviews of this verification document during the period of performance to determine if the process needs to be revised.

conditions: during the period of performance

This Departmental Manual (DM) establishes the process for how the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) manages licensed information technology (IT) software and how to determine payment for fewer or additional licenses using an annual reconciliation process, in accordance with the enterprise agreement between the vendor and USDA.

This DM applies to USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, volunteers, and others working for, or on behalf of, USDA who manage USDA-supplied computer hardware and software in the performance of their duties on behalf of USDA.

The Federal Government spends a significant amount annually on software acquisitions to enable business or mission functions.

a. The Federal Government spends a significant amount annually on software acquisitions to enable business or mission functions. It is incumbent on USDA to ensure practices as a purchaser and user of licensed software are carried out effectively, efficiently, and in compliance with all applicable legislation and copyrights, for example *Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act* (FITARA),  Public Law (P.L.) 113-291 § 831-837 ; *Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014* (FISMA),  44 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 3551 , et seq.; and Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Memorandum  M-16-12 , *Category Management Policy 16-1: Improving the Acquisition and Management of Common Information Technology: Software Licensing*.
